📰 General

Kennedy Center Faces Accusations of Deliberate Closure Following Legal Dispute •

The Kennedy Center is facing accusations from Representative Joyce Beatty that it is intentionally maintaining a state of closure following a court order. Beatty, a member of the venue’s board, alleges the center is allowing itself to become a “lifeless husk” by failing to reinstate regular performances and programming. The dispute stems from a legal challenge seeking to remove former President Trump’s name from the venue. The Kennedy Center maintains that the ongoing legal proceedings are the reason for the paused operations.

🌍 World

Spain’s Prime Minister’s Wife Ordered to Stand Trial in Corruption Case •

Spanish authorities have ordered Begona Gomez, the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, to face trial on corruption charges. The court ruling alleges she exploited her position as the government’s wife to obtain employment contracts. The charges relate to alleged misuse of her role to secure preferential treatment. The investigation is ongoing, and Gomez denies any wrongdoing.

🦅 US

Group F World Cup Battles Heat Up: Netherlands vs. Sweden Key Match Today •

Group F of the 2026 World Cup is proving to be highly competitive, featuring Japan, the Netherlands, and Sweden, all possessing the potential for advancement. Today’s match between Netherlands and Sweden is a crucial second-round game that will significantly impact the group’s standings. The game will determine whether these teams can continue their strong performances and contend for a place in the knockout stages. Analysts predict a closely contested match with significant implications for the group’s overall outcome.

💰 Business

Tesla Driver in Autopilot Mode Kills Woman in Texas House Crash •

A driver operating a Tesla Model 3 in what investigators believe was autopilot mode collided with a house in Texas on Friday evening. The crash resulted in the death of a woman who was inside the residence. Authorities are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident and the vehicle’s operational status at the time of the collision. The driver, Michael Butler, was transported to a local hospital for treatment.

💻 Technology

Seven iPhone Models Hit by Critical, Unfixable Security Vulnerability •

A newly discovered security flaw is affecting seven older iPhone models, posing a significant risk to user data. Cybersecurity experts at Paradigm Shift identified the vulnerability, which allows hackers to compromise Apple devices. The flaw’s complexity makes it impossible to patch with existing software updates. Affected models include iPhone 6, 6 Plus, SE (1st & 2nd generation), 7, 8, and X. Apple has not yet released a statement regarding the issue.

🎭 Entertainment

Zendaya Dominates Met Gala, Showcasing Stunning Custom Valentino Gown •

Zendaya attended the 2024 Met Gala in a breathtaking custom Valentino gown designed by Pierpaolo Piccioli. The dress featured a dramatic, floor-length silhouette with intricate embellishments and a deep V-neckline. She was joined by her partner, Tom Holland, who sported a tailored black suit. The event, themed "Sleeping Beauties: Reawakening Fashion," drew celebrities from across the entertainment industry.

🏅 Sports

Doku’s World Cup Departure Sparks Criticism Over Prioritizing Family •

Belgium winger Jeremy Doku announced his intention to leave the national team’s 2026 World Cup squad to be present for the birth of his first child. This decision has drawn criticism from teammates and national team staff who believe his absence would negatively impact the squad’s performance. The Belgian Football Association has not formally commented on the situation, but sources indicate they were not initially aware of Doku’s plans. The team is currently preparing for their group stage match against Ecuador.

🔬 Science

Venera 14’s Historic Landing: First Images Reveal Venus’s Brutal Surface •

On March 5, 1982, the Soviet Venera 14 lander successfully touched down on the surface of Venus, marking a significant achievement in planetary exploration. The spacecraft deployed a protective cap for its camera lens before immediately capturing images of the surrounding, rocky terrain. Venera 14 transmitted these photographs back to Earth, providing the first visual data from the planet’s surface. The mission was abruptly terminated due to extreme heat and pressure, highlighting the challenges of operating on Venus.

🩺 Health

New Study Links Gut Bacteria to Increased Risk of Alzheimer’s Disease •

Researchers at the University of Minnesota have identified a specific gut bacteria composition that correlates with an elevated risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease. The study, published in Alzheimer’s & Dementia, analyzed the gut microbiome of over 150 individuals, comparing those with and without the disease. Participants with a higher abundance of Desulfovibrio bacteria exhibited a significantly increased risk of cognitive decline. Scientists believe this bacteria produces compounds that can trigger inflammation in the brain, potentially contributing to the progression of Alzheimer’s.
